events.title: Battle of Stiklestad
events.description: King Olaf II of Norway was killed at Stiklestad while trying to win back his throne from Danish rule. His forces were defeated in the fighting.
events.significance: Olaf was later canonized as Saint Olaf and became Norway's eternal king. His cult helped consolidate Christianity in Scandinavia and shaped Norwegian national identity.

events.title: King Umberto I of Italy assassinated
events.description: In Monza, the Italian anarchist Gaetano Bresci shot and killed King Umberto I. Bresci said he acted to avenge the victims of a violent crackdown on protesters in Milan.
events.significance: The killing was one of several assassinations of heads of state around 1900. It brought Victor Emmanuel III to the throne, and his reign lasted through the rise of Italian Fascism.

events.title: London hosts the first postwar Summer Olympics
events.description: The Games of the XIV Olympiad opened in London. They were the first Olympics held since 1936, after the Second World War had cancelled the 1940 and 1944 Games.
events.significance: The 'Austerity Games' showed the world returning to peaceful competition. Athletes were housed in existing barracks and colleges rather than in a purpose-built village.

events.title: NASA is created
events.description: President Dwight D. Eisenhower signed the National Aeronautics and Space Act into law. It established the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.
events.significance: The new agency drove the American space program, including the Apollo Moon landings, and made space exploration a national priority during the Cold War.
